themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often shifts while you measure it. So the usual first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: On cross-channel incrementality the models call for always-on holdout markets and one trusted record of outcomes because platform behavior shifts under the test, and the same lack of an answer key drives answer engine optimization, identity resolution, and B2B buying-group intent signal.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. A shared schema or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: Cross-channel incrementality turns on platforms having no reason to expose auditable test assignment, agentic traffic on agents having reason to hide, journey orchestration on channel budgets rewarding sends, and the semantic context layer on departments defending their own numbers.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution draws proxies, brokers, and hard spend and audience caps from all three models, downstream consent work puts a single gate in front of every data exit, and journey orchestration proposes one shared pre-send check or contact ledger.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. Compliance and effects can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers say enforcement ends at the boundary of systems you do not control, and today's incrementality answers say the platforms control both the delivery and the evidence about it.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers converge on an approved-claims library because deciding whether wording breaks a claim stays a human reasoning task, and the semantic context layer answers say conflicting definitions of customer are a political settlement, not a schema.
